archetypes.name: Find an Inverse Rule for an Invertible Polynomial
archetypes.source: OpenStax Algebra and Trigonometry 2e §5.7 — Inverses and Radical Functions
archetypes.coreConcept: An inverse rule reverses the input-output relation of a one-to-one function; it is found by exchanging the variables and solving for the new output.
archetypes.mentalModel: Treat the original output as the new input, then undo the original operations in reverse order to recover the old input.
archetypes.governingRelation: y=f(x) ⇔ x=f^{-1}(y); after solving, rename y as x

cognitiveTraps.description: Treating inverse-function notation as a reciprocal of the function value.
Exchanging x and y but stopping before isolating the new output.

archetypes.figureNone: The item tests symbolic reversal of a one-to-one rule; a graph would not add information needed to solve it.

archetypes.name: Restrict a Polynomial Domain Before Finding Its Inverse
archetypes.source: OpenStax Algebra and Trigonometry 2e §5.7 — Inverses and Radical Functions
archetypes.coreConcept: A function that is not one-to-one on its full domain can become invertible after restricting its input set to a one-to-one branch.
archetypes.mentalModel: Keep one monotone branch of the original graph; the inverse then returns outputs only from that chosen branch.
archetypes.governingRelation: If f is restricted to D and one-to-one there, Range(f^{-1})=D

cognitiveTraps.description: Keeping both square-root branches even though the restricted original domain permits only one.
Choosing an inverse branch without matching the stated restricted domain.

archetypes.name: Find the Domain of a Radical Function
archetypes.source: OpenStax Algebra and Trigonometry 2e §5.7 — Inverses and Radical Functions
archetypes.coreConcept: An even-root expression is real only when its radicand is nonnegative; solving that condition determines its real domain.
archetypes.mentalModel: Treat the radicand as the quantity under a real square root and keep exactly the inputs that make it nonnegative.

cognitiveTraps.description: Excluding input values where an even-root radicand is exactly zero, even though the root is defined there.
cognitiveTraps.trapFormula: g(x)=0 is omitted from the domain even though sqrt(0) is real

cognitiveTraps.description: Reversing the accepted interval when solving a radicand inequality with a negative leading coefficient.
cognitiveTraps.trapFormula: for a downward quadratic radicand, keep the outside intervals instead of the interval between its roots

archetypes.figureNone: The prompt gives an algebraic radicand and asks for its domain; a graph would show the endpoint directly instead of testing the domain condition.

archetypes.name: Find the Inverse of a Radical Function
archetypes.source: OpenStax Algebra and Trigonometry 2e §5.7 — Inverses and Radical Functions
archetypes.coreConcept: A radical function can often be inverted by exchanging input and output and applying the matching power while preserving the function's domain and range restrictions.
archetypes.mentalModel: Undo the root with its corresponding power, then isolate the original input; check that the result reverses the stated mapping.
archetypes.governingRelation: If y=√[n]{g(x)}, then y^n=g(x), subject to the original domain and range

cognitiveTraps.description: Failing to apply the power that undoes a radical after exchanging variables.
Inverting a coefficient without also reversing the additive term.

archetypes.figureNone: The item asks for an algebraic inverse rule, not graph reconstruction; an expression check verifies the reversal.

archetypes.name: Verify an Inverse Pair with Composition
archetypes.source: OpenStax Algebra and Trigonometry 2e §5.7 — Inverses and Radical Functions
archetypes.coreConcept: Two functions are inverses when composing them in either order returns the original input on the relevant domains.
archetypes.mentalModel: Feed an output through the proposed undo rule and then return through the original rule; each direction should restore its starting input.
archetypes.governingRelation: g(f(x))=x and f(g(x))=x on their respective domains

cognitiveTraps.description: Checking only one composition and overlooking a failure in the reverse order.
Substituting the two functions in an order different from the composition requested.

archetypes.figureNone: Composition is a symbolic substitution check; a figure would not determine whether both identities hold.
